header.title: Level 4: hedging with other products, and holding risk overnight
header.briefing: It is late afternoon and you are carrying a 5Y client position. Swaps are expensive to trade this late; futures are not. A hedge is a trade: choose the product by its cost, the risk it leaves (swap spread, futures basis), what it carries overnight and how long you will hold it.

input.hint: 'none'; '100% 10y' (of your DV01); 'flatten' (level, slope and curvature); or legs: 'pay 150m 10y + receive 60m 30y'; futures and bonds: 'sell 300 fgbl', 'buy 120 fgbm', 'sell 50m ctd'; 'switch' closes product hedges into swaps

reasons: Clearly beaten: another choice costs less, or removes much more risk for little extra cost, whatever your risk appetite. For a middle-of-the-range appetite the best balance is: hedge level and curve (10y + 2y).
Your choice: cost now €25,000, risk over the next step sigma €44,828 (keeping the book as it is: sigma €232,118).
You are left with swap-spread risk: -347,476 EUR per bp of ASW tightening. Futures and bonds hedge rates, but they are not swaps: if bonds cheapen against swaps your hedge underperforms.

header.title: Level 4: hedging with other products, and holding risk overnight
notes: Morning: swap liquidity is back. Review the hedges you carried.

risk_card.title: Training assumptions (a simplified model for this exercise, not estimates of true market volatility)

conditions.flow: morning: the swap market is deep again.

observation.prompt: Liquidity is back. Re-hedge, switch, or keep your hedges as they are?

input.hint: 'none'; '100% 10y' (of your DV01); 'flatten' (level, slope and curvature); or legs: 'pay 150m 10y + receive 60m 30y'; futures and bonds: 'sell 300 fgbl', 'buy 120 fgbm', 'sell 50m ctd'; 'switch' closes product hedges into swaps

decision.label: Switch the product hedges into 5Y swaps

reasons: A reasonable trade-off for a reasonable risk appetite. For a middle-of-the-range appetite the best balance is: switch the product hedges into 5y swaps.
Your choice: cost now €40,188, risk over the next step sigma €52,211 (keeping the book as it is: sigma €82,642).
You are left with a curve position: +40,492 EUR per bp of slope. A DV01 hedge in another tenor hedges the level, not the curve.
Client flow over the rest of the day should net away roughly 90% of what you keep: that is the case for warehousing it rather than paying to hedge it now.
